title: 1988 AHSME Problem 16
statement: \(ABC\) and \(A'B'C'\) are equilateral triangles with parallel sides and the same center, as in the figure. The distance between side \(BC\) and side \(B'C'\) is \(\frac16\) the altitude of \(\triangle ABC.\) The ratio of the area of \(\triangle A'B'C'\) to the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is

solutions.text:
Let the outer and inner altitudes be \(h\) and \(h'.\) Their common center is \(\frac{h}{3}\) above \(BC\) and \(\frac{h'}{3}\) above \(B'C'.\) Hence \(\frac{h-h'}{3}=\frac{h}{6},\) so \(h'=\frac{h}{2}.\) Areas scale as the square of corresponding lengths, giving \((\frac{h'}{h})^2=\frac{1}{4}.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: A centroid lies one-third of the altitude above the base
Relate the two altitudes using the distance between their parallel bases
